original_test_intent: Validate that one approved reversible Advanced Power Management change persists across reboot and that authorized project defaults restore qualified power, frequency, idle and thermal behavior without throttling, protection loss, hang or crash.
original_method: Bind platform, BIOS, CPU, BMC and power/cooling identity; preserve baseline logs and telemetry; drain workloads; an operator changes one dependency-aware reversible APM control through KVM, saves/reboots, verifies retention and its measured effect, then uses the approved restore path and proves the project menu plus power/frequency/idle/thermal/fan/protection state returns; stop on limit excursion, persistent throttling, boot failure or management loss.
manual_activity: A qualified BIOS/power operator applies this row's approved APM change and restore through KVM while supervising power and thermal behavior.
required_inputs: Platform/BIOS/CPU/BMC/power/cooling identity and exact APM page semantics
Project/factory APM defaults and one safe reversible dependency-aware value
Power, frequency, idle-state, thermal, throttle, fan and protection telemetry oracle
Maintenance/KVM, workload drain and physical/CMOS recovery ownership
safety_requirements: Never use all/random values or disable thermal/power protections
Preserve logs and keep this row's evidence independent from row 2182
Drain workloads and continuously observe approved power/thermal limits
Stop on limit excursion, unstable power state, persistent throttling, POST failure or management-path loss
No automatic retry or unapproved CMOS clear
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, project-default semantics, APM dependencies, telemetry thresholds and recovery
Collect row-specific baseline/retained/restored power and thermal evidence
Guide KVM checkpoints and compare state without verdict
Do not choose/change BIOS values, disable protections, clear logs, reuse other evidence or invoke recovery
engineer_actions: Approve independent change-default scope and project/factory APM oracle
Approve the reversible value, monitoring limits, aborts and recovery
Review this row's evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH MANUAL APM CHANGE-DEFAULT AND POWER-STATE RESTORATION TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use one platform-owner-approved reversible APM value and prove retained/restored menu plus measured power, frequency, idle, thermal and protection state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds variant isolation, project-default semantics, dependency-aware value selection, workload drain, telemetry limits and recovery.

modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Unsafe APM values can destabilize power states, degrade performance, overheat components, trigger throttling or prevent boot.

This variant's project/factory APM oracle, reversible value, dependencies and limits

Timestamp-aligned power, frequency, idle-state, thermal, throttle, fan and protection telemetry
Preserved SEL, kernel, boot/POST evidence plus workload-drain record

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2189 Wistron-BIOS-00506-V002: define this change-default variant's independent coverage and project-versus-factory APM restore target; approve platform/BIOS/CPU/BMC/power/cooling identity, one safe reversible dependency-aware value replacing `all/random`, power/frequency/idle/thermal/throttle/fan/protection criteria, workload drain, telemetry/log preservation, aborts, and KVM/physical/CMOS recovery ownership.

review_improvement: Preserves independent APM change-default coverage and connects restored BIOS values to measurable platform power and thermal safety.
independent_technical_reasoning: APM menu persistence alone does not prove the requested behavior because dependent firmware policy can change frequency, idle residency, thermal response and protection state. This variant requires one understood reversible value, an effective telemetry oracle and separate evidence from row 2182. Workloads must be drained, limits monitored throughout, and any excursion or unstable boot must terminate the manual action without retry.
